chapter: Duke, Gensel and the later years
title: The Tribute to Charlie Parker tour with Sonny Stitt
summary: Newport's Bird tribute went to Europe; McGhee and Stitt drank heavily.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Anyway, we'll come back to that. I remember the Tribute to Bird. You had Sonny Stitt, yourself and J.J., and you played...
Oh, Kenny Clarke, right. Then you toured Europe with that.

Yeah, we went to Europe. We did a TV show in London; what's his name got that one.

Do you want to know what happened to the tour, or what happened on the tour, or...?
Well, if there's anything that you remember.

Well, I remember that we... I was drinking quite a bit at that stage, and so was Sonny. And we used to be drinking buddies; we'd go to bed together and get up together, you know, and drink together -- which was horrible, in a sense, because you can't do that... You think you're doing something when you're drunk, but you're not. You're not like your real self.

Anyway, so that's what was happening back at that stage. It was a nice affair, the Tribute to Charlie Parker show. I mean, it was a good idea of George's to put that on. Well, we only did I think one tour with that group overseas. Then I don't know what happened ...(?)... when we came back to the States. Everybody went their own way.
Do you have something you wanted on that?
